G1.name: Clarify
G1.approves: The user stories and their numbered acceptance criteria

G2.name: Refine / Align
G2.approves: The frozen spec, read after the architecture narrative

G3.name: Plan
G3.note: The human may delegate this gate to the orchestrator for small plans.

release.name: Release go / no-go
release.approves: The product-owner's go / no-go on the release scope and the release-gate checklist

AI-DLC.name: Full lifecycle
AI-DLC.pickWhen: A feature, epic or idea must go from intent to release (the default for feature work)
AI-DLC.exitArtifact: A released (or release-ready) feature, traceable brief -> stories / ACs -> ADRs / spec -> tasks -> code / tests / docs -> review report -> release notes
AI-DLC.note: Enter at the earliest missing artifact and run to the end. FDLC runs once per task or wave of tasks. Re-anchor on the frozen spec at every boundary after G2. Executed as request-routing Mode 4, full lifecycle traversal.

PDLC.name: Product Design
PDLC.pickWhen: The input is a vague idea, epic or business goal
PDLC.exitArtifact: Feature list, use-case diagrams, user stories with numbered ACs in docs/product/ and docs/backlog/backlog.md

stages.note: Outcomes, features, use cases; returns a delegation list for requirement-analyst and product-manager.

produces: User stories with testable, numbered ACs in docs/product/
stages.note: One question at a time until every story has testable, numbered ACs.
Backlog entries with the priority the product-owner decided.

produces: Acceptance of the stories and the backlog

loop.on: The product-owner sends the stories or the backlog back

ASDLC.name: Architecture & Design
ASDLC.pickWhen: Stories exist but no agreed design / spec
ASDLC.exitArtifact: ADRs in docs/architecture/decisions/ plus a frozen docs/specs/<slug>.spec.md per story, co-owned by software-architect and system-engineer

stages.note: Each consequential decision becomes an ADR.

stages.when: the design depends on an external fact (library, API, standard) the team has not verified
stages.note: Runs in parallel with the architecture stage.
software-architect and system-engineer co-sign the spec; it is then frozen. Changes after freezing go back through this stage.
The three-act story (problem -> constraints and trade-offs -> design, ADRs, risks), written for the human who approves G2.

STBLC.name: Story & Task Breakdown
STBLC.pickWhen: A frozen spec exists but no task plan
STBLC.exitArtifact: docs/plans/<slug>.tasks.md: estimated, dependency-ordered tasks, each with its own technical Definition of Done

stages.note: Splits the frozen spec into tasks; each task records id, AC references, dependencies, estimate and technical DoD.
Co-splits with software-architect at the low-level design boundaries.

produces: Estimates and flagged unknowns in the task plan

FDLC.name: Feature Development
FDLC.pickWhen: Tasks exist and code must land
FDLC.exitArtifact: Merge-ready change: code, tests, docs, review report with zero Blockers
FDLC.note: The build loop. Runs once per task or wave of tasks.

produces: Green build and tests (the project's commands)
stages.note: Every behaviour traces to a numbered AC; anything outside the spec goes back to ASDLC.
AI-driven UI tests run through the Playwright MCP tools.

loop.on: A test or the mutation run reveals a defect in production code (Quality Check & Refinement)

stages.note: Also the stack's unit, integration, UI and mutation-testing skills (csharp-* or ts-*). Unit, integration and UI suites may fan out to parallel sqa-engineer instances.

produces: Updated README.md files for every changed component

loop.on: The change does not conform to the ADRs or the spec (Architecture Conformance)

produces: Severity-ranked findings report with zero Blockers

loop.on: Blockers in the review report; Blockers in test code go to the tests stage (Code Audit & Refinement)

stages.note: Fanned out to one code-reviewer per review axis.

BFLC.name: Bug Fixing
BFLC.exitArtifact: Root cause statement, minimal fix, a regression test that failed before and passes after

stages.note: fix-bug Phase 1 only. research-assistant if external behaviour is involved; software-architect if the cause is architectural.

stages.when: the bug is a security issue
stages.note: Run before the fix lands; notify the product-owner afterwards.

produces: Regression test passes, full suite green

RLC.name: Refactoring
RLC.pickWhen: Structure must change, behaviour must not
RLC.exitArtifact: Refactor diff, unchanged public behaviour, mutation score not lower than baseline

stages.note: The stack's mutation-testing skill, baseline mode, before any change.
Defined together with system-engineer.
Small steps, tests green after each.

produces: Mutation report not lower than the baseline

loop.on: The mutation score regressed below the baseline

produces: Findings report confirming no behaviour change

TLC.name: Testing
TLC.pickWhen: Existing code lacks coverage, AC traceability or mutation strength
TLC.exitArtifact: Test plan, new tests, AC-traceability table, mutation report

produces: Test plan with an AC-traceability table

stages.note: Also the stack's mutation-testing skill. software-engineer touches production code only if a test reveals a bug, which forks a BFLC item.

CRLC.name: Code Review
CRLC.pickWhen: An open change / PR must be driven to merge-ready
CRLC.exitArtifact: Findings report; code-reviewer approves only at zero Blockers

loop.on: Fixes go back to review until zero Blockers remain

stages.note: sqa-engineer addresses Blockers in test code; the product-owner resolves scope disputes. The orchestrator verifies and reports at zero Blockers.

AAW.name: Agent Artifact Work
AAW.pickWhen: The request changes agents, skills, hooks, rules / instructions, commands / prompts, agent memory or the workflow file (agent-artifact work)
AAW.exitArtifact: The changed agent artifacts, their platform checks green, a PASS from brutal-critique on the docs, and passing tests and a clean code review on the code
AAW.note: No work breakdown, no gates and no handoff records; the run state records each round and links every hand-back, and both are committed when the run closes. Change kinds (code or docs), what a round is and which findings start one: the workflow skill's references/aaw-review.md. The maxRounds of the three review loops are one shared budget, not one per loop: validate requires them equal. A change to agent-manager's own definition, or to a skill it owns, is made by a freshly spawned agent-manager, never by a running instance.

produces: The changed paths, each marked code or docs
The checks run and their results
stages.note: Uses the management skill for each artifact kind; ends with the twin or build checks (harness-sync --check, or the plugin build --check). The orchestrator re-runs those checks before any review.

produces: Critique of the docs in the change set with a PASS / REVISE verdict

loop.on: A REVISE verdict, or Majors on a PASS: the critique goes back to agent-manager with the same changed paths and intent

stages.note: Reviews the docs paths against the intent, using the skill-management writing guide; read-only.

produces: The test run and its results

loop.on: A test that fails because the code is wrong: the failure goes back to agent-manager

stages.note: Writes or updates tests for the code paths against the intent, in the repository's test folder outside the shipped plugin, with the repository's test runner (or the stack's built-in one), and runs them. The tests join the change set as code.

produces: Severity-ranked findings on the code and its tests

loop.on: A Blocker or Warning: the findings go back to agent-manager

stages.note: Reviews the code paths and the new tests against the intent (standards axis); read-only.
Also the stack's package-deployment skill (nuget-package-deployment or npm-package-deployment).

product-owner.about: release-gate checklist status before go / no-go
everything else is intent, asked through the orchestrator

requirement-analyst.about: test seams, boundaries and data shapes while drafting the spec they co-sign
test seams, boundaries and data shapes while drafting the spec they co-sign

product-manager.about: scope, priority, milestone and release decisions
stories and ACs being sliced into work items

software-architect.about: at Architecture Conformance, the intent behind the diff
at Architecture Conformance, the intent behind the design

system-engineer.about: architecture, boundaries, ADR intent, and every decision that would change the architecture (escalated, never made)

software-engineer.about: low-level design, patterns, UI design, interfaces
the meaning of an AC in the spec

sqa-engineer.about: implementation details and the test cases the change implies
system design and test-case design (seams, interfaces)
architecture testing (layer and dependency rules, NFRs)

documentation-writer.about: behaviour and public API of the change

code-reviewer.about: the meaning of an AC on the spec axis

devops-engineer.about: conditions attached to the go / no-go
